maria: Pushing the profiler dump for prefix/prompt cache from the 9am canary run. Big delta by deployment type, putting raw numbers below.

maria: ```
prefix_cache.summary {
  hosted: { hit_rate: 0.68, avg_latency_ms: 1.9, keys: 12k }
  dedicated: { hit_rate: 0.44, avg_latency_ms: 2.3, keys: 18k }
  private: { hit_rate: 0.26, avg_latency_ms: 8.7, keys: 42k }
}
```

jevon: Wow private is terrible. Is this latency due to NFS? or just fragmentation of keys?

sasha: First guess: key churn / different normalization across deployments. Hosted/Dedicated had the prefix-normalize change applied in the rollout pipeline; some Private installs still running pre-normalize behavior.

maria: Yeah, I diffed key samples. Hosted/Dedicated keys look like `model:v2|q8|norm:abc123|prompt_hash:fff` but Private nodes have `session=...|model:v2|raw_prompt` in many entries. So smaller hit-rate and many large values stored on NFS.

zane: For private we've got cache directory mounted over NFS in most customer AMIs. That adds 4-10ms per lookup + higher risk of stale mounts. Also some VPC setups block our discovery traffic so the cache sharding falls back to a per-process namespace leading to duplication.

eli: Is this a regression tied to the recent prefix key change we shipped last week (commit 1745xx)?

maria: Correlation looks strong. Dedicated picked up the new default config via infra bootstrap; Private installs with config drift didn't. So the same logical prompt ends up with two different key shapes depending on config parity.

jevon: Ok. Immediate mitigation ideas?

sasha: 1) Add deployment_type tag to prefix_cache metrics and emit key-churn (unique keys/sec) so we can surface it in console.

sasha: 2) Hotfix: accept both old and new key formats for 48h during rollouts (double-lookup) to avoid cold-miss storms.

eli: 3) Warmup job: leaderboard of top prompts per model/region, background worker populates KV on rollout. Something like:

eli: ```bash
# pseudo
curl -X POST $CONTROLPLANE/rollout/warmpop 
  -d '{"model":"moss-1","top_k":200,"deployment_type":"private"}'
```

maria: 4) In Private, fall back to in-memory LRU if filesystem latency > 5ms. That avoids the 8ms tail for small prefixes.

zane: Infrastructure note: for customers with VPC constraints we should document recommended mount options (noac, actimeo=1) and a supported local-ssd fallback. Ops: we already have an internal KB link but it's sparse.

maria: I'll open a ticket and assign: infra/ops to update the AMI and docs, runtime to implement double-lookup compatibility and metric tags, jobs to build a warmup task. Patch plan:
- runtime: add key compatibility layer + metric tag (PR -> canary)
- infra: AMI image with updated mount_opts + local cache daemon
- devex: add console charts (prefix_cache.hit_rate by deployment_type)
- ops: run warmup for affected customers during next maintenance window

deploy-bot: Deployed canary with "key-compatibility" branch to us-west-2 canary pool at 1752109950 :white_check_mark:

jevon: Nice. For the longer term we should standardize canonical key tuple: `model@version|quant|prefix_norm_vN|prompt_hash` and a migration plan that avoids double growth of keys.

sasha: Agreed. Also need a perf test that simulates NFS-backed KV with realistic latencies so we don't regress when teams flip configs.

eli: Action items taken: I'll add the metrics tags and heatmap panels. Maria can you open the ticket and list customers impacted (patch IDs)?

maria: On it, will post ticket + initial list in #customer-success. Thanks all :thumbsup:

zane: Quick follow-up: can we also capture top-10 long tails for private (prompts that never hit)? helps tune warmup.

maria: Yep adding that to the ticket now.

jevon: Good triage. If we can get the double-lookup hotfix out within 6 hours we should avoid a broader cold start spike during peak.

sasha: I'll pick up the hotfix PR review.

eli: I'll prototype warmup job tomorrow morning.

maria: Thanks team. Closing thread after ticket posted.
